title: Vue watchers and async search without stale state
outcome: Implement a watched request with cleanup, current-result guards, and honest loading/error states.
useCase: Live ticket search and dependent selects.
benefits: Predictable async state under fast input.
drawbacks: Cancellation, ownership, and validation need separate handling.
version: Modern JavaScript / TypeScript · Vue 3.5 where applicable · browser APIs
cue: Cleanup revokes ownership, not just network work.

trace.title: Reactive query
trace.detail:
## Understand the idea

Use watch when you want a side effect tied to a specific source. watchEffect tracks reactive reads made during its synchronous execution; reads after the first await do not automatically become dependencies of that effect.

Register cancellation before awaiting. Vue 3.5 onWatcherCleanup must be called synchronously.

The watch callback’s onCleanup argument is a useful alternative. Cleanup means the old request no longer owns this view, even if the network cannot be cancelled immediately.

Keep state transitions explicit. A stale response must not publish rows, an error, or loading=false.

Decide whether an empty query clears results. Debouncing reduces request frequency but does not establish response order.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
Query A starts and owns active=true. Query B invalidates A: cleanup sets A inactive and aborts it.

B becomes the owner. If A finishes later, its active check prevents every visible update.

Test success-success in reverse order, stale failure after success, abort, and unmount. Give each request a controlled deferred response so the test chooses the timeline.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail: Putting onWatcherCleanup after await can miss the synchronous registration requirement. Debouncing alone still allows two requests to overlap.
